text:
matt: Heads-up — us-west1 spot GPU availability has been degrading for the last 3h. Prod low-latency pool saw 2x preemptions in the last hour and p95 encode latency spiked past 350ms.
sana: Which pool exactly? prod-lowlatency or batch-spot?
matt: prod-lowlatency. We're currently using price-optimized bids.
lee: Price-optimized gives cheaper runs but is fragile during market churn. Capacity-optimized usually trades ~5-12% extra cost for stability.
emily: Our SLA: allowed cost variance up to 10% if p95 latency stays <250ms. Right now the latency increase means we should prioritize availability.
juan: Suggest a mixed approach: 70% capacity-optimized, 30% price-optimized. That keeps cost down during calm periods and buys stability when markets are rough.
matt: Ops log: `asg scale-up failed: Insufficient capacity in zone a` — we retried but got more preemptions after provisioning.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Autoscaler retried 3x, warm buffer is empty for prod-lowlatency. Recommendation: maintain warm_nodes >=1 per AZ.
sana: Warm buffer sounds right. Do we prefer one warm per region or per AZ (to avoid cross-AZ failovers)?
lee: Per-AZ warm node reduces cross-AZ traffic and tail risk. Downside: small extra baseline cost and slightly higher replication/egress. Proposal: `warm_nodes_per_az=1`, `warm_ttl=15m`.
juan: Also pin warm nodes to cheaper GPU SKUs that are compatible (same family) so GPU context loads fine. Eg. use smaller instance shape for warm holder.
emily: If we switch to capacity-optimized, we need to retune the eviction handler. Currently it tries immediate reschedule which fails when capacity is low — we should add exponential backoff and spillback logic.
matt: Proposal: change bid_strategy to `hybrid_capacity_weighted` with params: weight_capacity=0.7, max_price_delta_pct=10, and explicit fallback_zones list.
lee: Example config patch for the spot pool: 
```json
{
  "bid_strategy": "hybrid_capacity_weighted",
  "capacity_weight": 0.7,
  "max_price_delta_pct": 10,
  "warm_nodes_per_az": 1,
  "warm_ttl_minutes": 15,
  "fallback_zones": ["us-west1-b","us-west1-c"]
}
```
juan: Nice. We should also add a circuit-breaker: if spot_eviction_rate > 3% sustained for 5m, failover X% traffic to `dedicated-pool`. Suggest X=20 for first stage.
emily: Agree. Add an alert in console: `spot_fail_rate` and `spot_cost_delta_pct`. Also a dashboard cell for p95 encode latency by pool.
sana: How will we measure cost impact? Finance wants to be notified if monthly spend delta > $6k. Add an automated Slack alert to #finance-ops if projected delta exceeds threshold.
matt: I'll run a 30m canary in us-west1 with the new params starting at 2401122400. Will monitor p95 and eviction rate.
lee: I’ll update terraform module `infra/gpu/spot_pools.tf` and open a PR with the config. Will include `canary=true` flag.
juan: One more: consider cross-region spillback ordering. If all AZs in us-west1 degrade, we should prefer us-central1 capacity-optimized before shifting to on-demand/dedicated in region — that preserves latency.
emily: Add rule: `if region_eviction_pct > 10% for 5m -> route 50% to us-central1 capacity-optimized, 50% to dedicated fallback` in rollout policy.
matt: SGTM. I'll push the PR and schedule the canary. If p95 improves and eviction_rate drops under 1.5% within 30m, we'll roll to full region.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started at 2401122400 (canary id: canary-240112). Will post metrics to #eng-metrics.
lee: FYI I added a short-run script to simulate preemption handling locally: `scripts/test-eviction.sh --nodes 10 --preempt-rate 0.2` — can help validate backoff logic.
juan: Finance pinged: looping @finance-team if the PR shows cost delta > $6k projected.
matt: :thumbsup: thanks team. Will update thread with canary results in ~45m and follow-up with a short postmortem if anything odd.
